rationale: The configured generic extcon framework must not reuse a connector ID until device_unregister has removed its device name. The release callback in pinned LTS is empty and object storage has separate ownership, so moving ida_free afterward does not dereference freed extcon storage. This prevents registration collisions without changing LTS lifetime rules.

The SDK uses ext4 and enables Unicode/casefold support. Pinned LTS still invalidates a casefolded dentry while holding a journal handle; eviction of child dentries can wait on that transaction, causing a deadlock. Stop the transaction before d_invalidate and guard invalidation on successful removal. The cherry-pick preserves all other newer LTS namei fixes and closes an availability failure.

F2FS remains enabled for Android configuration compatibility. Pinned LTS has the inline-directory conversion bounds check but lacks this lookup check. Reject an on-disk name length above F2FS_NAME_LEN or extending past the available filename slots before comparing it. This prevents out-of-bounds reads from malformed directory entries; existing LTS error cleanup and inode validation are unchanged.

The configured block scheduler permits concurrent sysfs scheduler changes. Pinned LTS retains the two-stage elevator_change/elevator_change_done sequence and a shared read lock, which permits concurrent kobject cleanup and memory corruption. Use the writer trylock for the whole switch, retaining the LTS trylock/EBUSY behavior that avoids the kernfs disk-deletion lock cycle.

ARM64-specific additions are excluded. Native LTS crypto fixes outside the selected series remain. Associated KUnit sources are retained but were not executed or enabled by the SDK build; no runtime claim is made. SECURITY.md records the known SDK AES-CTS storage policy and unresolved alternative HCTR2 use.

This intermediate rename allowed the old crypto_shash implementation to coexist with the new library during migration. The selected final series removes that old implementation entirely; the rename has no independent residual code or runtime requirement.

F2FS is enabled for Android filesystem compatibility. Propagate sync/checkpoint failures through directory-synchronous operations and a read-only remount instead of reporting success. In remount, clear SBI_IS_CLOSE before testing the sync error, preserving native LTS cleanup on failure before restore_gc. This avoids concealing durability failures without retaining an erroneous close-state flag.

In ra_data_block and move_data_block, LTS already acquires i_sem and igrab of the atomic inode before using its mapping, then iputs on success/error. Eviction uses the matching write lock before clearing the COW link. The port retains this protection together with its vendor bypass hooks.

LTS is_meta_ino already gates the synthetic compressed-cache inode on CONFIG_F2FS_FS_COMPRESSION and the COMPRESS_CACHE mount option. The port retains that check and the later rejection of inaccessible cached meta inodes.
LTS f2fs_move_file_range already stores the destination size as loff_t, checks LLONG_MAX overflow and calls inode_newsize_ok before extension. The port retains these checks with native LTS locking.

LTS already has do_zero_post_eof_page and the strict-mode writeback/error-return paths before size extension. Preserve its zeroing and writeback ordering to avoid stale post-EOF data after recovery; the ACK locking-context refactor is not required for this fix.

LTS __write_node_folio already passes folio->index to f2fs_sanity_check_node_footer, rather than comparing the node ID to itself. The port retains native LTS critical-error handling and this independent footer validation.

The pinned LTS already provides the transaction-lock snapshot and temporary target-thread reference in binder_free_transaction. Retain Rust Binder reference cleanup outside the node_refs spinlock: declare cleanup owners before the lock guard, remove rbtree nodes with remove_node, and preserve death/freeze cleanup until after unlocking. Retain the Rust Binder freeze-listener allocation retry: drop node_refs_guard before GFP_KERNEL vector allocation, reacquire and revalidate handle/cookie before modifying state, and defer the empty vector returned by remove_freeze_listener until outside the lock. This prevents sleeping allocation/free under the node_refs spinlock and retains freeze notification semantics.

LTS already keys its append-only mk_mode_keys list by HKDF context, cipher mode, data-unit size and encryption implementation. The SDK enables BLK_INLINE_ENCRYPTION_FALLBACK and DM_DEFAULT_KEY; native LTS __submit_bio invokes crypto preparation while current->bio_list is active, so recursive encrypted submissions can hold the resources an allocation awaits. Adapt the ACK rescue-list/workqueue fix to native per-page LTS allocation: nonblocking bio/page allocation in recursive submission, enqueue remaining source with its updated DUN, and retry outside recursion. When a partially filled bounce bio exhausts pages, submit it with an extra source completion reference before continuing; only an empty worker bio may block. This avoids both recursive-submit deadlock and waiting on pages held by the current partial bio without importing the bulk-mempool refactor. Preserve early LTS alignment validation, on-stack requests, native completion/error behavior and dm-default-key skip-bit propagation. Availability/security rationale and compile-only verification limits are in SECURITY.md.

Retain the ACK separation of pre-metadata resize failure from post-update failure. This intentionally narrows the LTS repair flag to the error paths that can need repair, improving availability without suppressing detected corruption. The configured F2FS shrinker now checks freed < nr before reclaiming read-extent entries, just as it already does before NAT and free-NID reclamation. No memory-safety improvement or measured performance gain is claimed.

F2FS compression and filesystem encryption are enabled. In the compressed-write error unwind, skip fscrypt bounce-page finalization if fio.encrypted is false; retain normal context/page cleanup. Native LTS f2fs_gc_range accepts the lock argument, takes/releases gc_lock per section when requested, releases it on error/skip paths, and preserves early termination. Reviewed original three-line patch and native kvm_mmu_invalidate_mmio_sptes. This skips invalidation only when MMIO caching is disabled, avoiding unnecessary all-page zapping on rare generation wrap. Native LTS already performs safe invalidation and the change is a performance optimization, not a missing correctness/security fix. The pKVM backend which disables MMIO caching is excluded for this supplied SDK target. Retain LTS behavior to minimize unrelated changes; generic KVM and MMIO caching remain supported.
